set: B: seven sheets of consecutive frames at the slabs' drops and one at the hit on the arrow

issues.where: ‘Field cannot be blank,’ 2:00.13 to 2:00.50; the same motion recurs on ‘Invalid input’ in set-B-04.png and set-B-07.png
issues.what: The blocks travel diagonally in near-equal steps and stop in open space. The arrow, slot and surrounding page give no cue for what stopped them, so the supposed hits read as slides rather than impacts.
issues.fix: Give the blocks a short acceleration into a visible stop. On the contact frame, arrest the block, kick the struck part and carry a brief reaction into the page before holding.

issues.where: Arrow tip and left edge of ‘Invalid input,’ 2:09.20 to 2:09.37
issues.what: This is the strongest approach and reaction, but the arrow starts to twist away before the block reaches its nearest point. A gap remains as the block stops, and the glowing streak continues along the same line, so it is unclear what hit the arrow.
issues.fix: Make the intended striker visibly meet the arrow on a single frame. Tie the arrow’s recoil, the striker’s stop or deflection, and the local flash to that contact, then hold the aftermath.

issues.where: ‘Required field’ approaching the left glass panel around 2:01.77; repeated in set-B-06.png around 2:04.23
issues.what: The block eases to rest just short of the panel with no matching reaction. The bright effect or movement at the far-right linkage does not read as an answer to that near-contact.
issues.fix: Show the block make contact with the glass frame and stop over a frame or two. Give that frame or its mounting a small, immediate jolt; cue any linkage action from the same hit if it is meant to be connected.

issues.where: ‘Session expired’ landing on the cracked slot around 2:01.60; repeated in set-B-05.png around 2:03.83
issues.what: The dust makes this landing readable, but the rim and cracked face remain visually locked when the block seats. The impacted side gives little sense of taking the load.
issues.fix: Keep the dust, add a tight contact shadow and a one-frame jolt to the slot lip or nearby debris, then let the rim settle while the block holds.
